title: Uncovering latent consensus in heterogeneous populations: The Mixture Linear Ordering Problem
summary: The classical linear ordering problem seeks a single ranking representing a given preference matrix. While suitable for homogeneous populations, it fails when observed preferences arise from several latent groups with distinct ranking patterns. To address this limitation, we introduce an extension partitioning the population into latent groups, each characterized by its own linear order, relative size, and preference structure.
